How to rate

Use headphones. Play the target melody first: it is a plain tone sequence, seven or eight notes at 120 BPM. Then play versions A, B and C.

Follows melody asks whether the music's melody moves through the same notes, in the same order and at roughly the same time as the target. Sound quality asks whether the clip sounds like clean, plausible music regardless of the melody.

Finally pick the version that follows the target best. Ratings save automatically once all three versions of an item are rated.

Where ratings go. On this public page your ratings stay in your own browser (local storage) and are never sent anywhere; they are not part of the paper, which uses no human ratings. Taking the test is voluntary.

All six items saved. Thank you.

You can revise any rating; changes are saved again automatically. The Labeled demo tab now reveals which version was which.

Clips are 5-second generations from Stable Audio Open 1.0 (50 EDM-DPM-solver steps, classifier-free guidance 4.0) and, in the second block, from the Stable Audio 3 medium base checkpoint (50 Euler steps, classifier-free guidance 7), downsampled to 22.05 kHz mono for the page. Prompts are held-out test captions; melodies are sequences of seven or eight quarter notes at 120 BPM.

All guided versions use the same budget of 15 probe updates and the same update rule; they differ only in which sampling steps are guided. Condition labels follow the paper: MLSP window = every second step from 20 to 48 (the schedule of the prior work); SCPG = the 15 steps where a single steering burst changes melodic coherence most, measured once per model on development prompts (steps 19–33 on Stable Audio Open, 4–18 on Stable Audio 3), shown here with reliability-scaled strength on both models.
